title: Finland orders halt to work on Google data centre sites
source_used: Al Jazeera (carries AFP and Reuters material); text from WORKDIR/fulltext/C09-02.txt
key_facts: The Finnish Supervisory Agency (LVV) ordered Tuike Finland, the company acting for Google, to suspend preparatory work at planned data center sites in Muhos and Kajaani no later than 23 Oct 2026.
The order stands until compulsory environmental impact assessments are done.

LVV was investigating whether hundreds of hectares of forest were cleared without the required assessment; its environment head Tommi Muilu says trees were removed, topsoil stripped, roads and storage areas built and ditches altered.
The Finnish Association for Nature Conservation says more than 300 hectares were deforested.
Tuike Finland must explain how it will proceed by 14 Oct; it could face enforcement proceedings if it does not comply.
A Google spokesman acknowledged shortcomings and said it would follow LVV's guidance.
Google announced in September a 13 billion euro investment in Finland over two years, its biggest in Europe.
quote_evidence: A Finnish government authority has ordered work on two Google data centre sites to stop until compulsory environmental impact assessments have been completed.
Tuike Finland must provide an explanation and detail how it intends to proceed by October 14.
It could face “enforcement proceedings” if it fails to comply, LVV said.
why_it_matters_hint: A regulator has moved from investigating to ordering a halt on part of Google's biggest European data center plan.
notes: Follow-up: the investigation was in our 6 Oct 2026 edition (AFP report of 4 Oct, relayed by Daily Sabah and Tom's Hardware). New today is the formal order.
